issues.problem: viprarṣi is 'brahmin sage' (vipra + ṛṣi); ब्रह्मर्षि renders a different word (brahmarṣi). English has it right.
'मुनि' is not in verse 7 (muniḥ comes only in verse 8); the English correctly says 'the mighty one'.
purāṇaḥ here is the adjective 'ancient'; in Hindi 'पुराण' reads as the Purāṇa texts.
Gloss 'of the Viśva (all-)' is garbled; the word is the pronoun/adjective viśva 'all', used here as the fixed name of the Viśve (devāḥ).
div 'heaven/sky' is feminine (dyauḥ, divam, divā); label says m.
The line can equally be construed 'and the Rākṣasas who were described as Duryodhana's allies' (parikīrtitāḥ with sahāyāḥ as predicate); the draft chose one construal without noting the other.

patch.text: Alternative construal: 'and the Rākṣasas who were described as allies of Duryodhana' (parikīrtitāḥ predicating duryodhana-sahāyāḥ); the sense is the same group either way.

issues.problem: The adverb reading ('assuredly'; also 'regularly, constantly') is acceptable and the supplied verb is honestly noted, but the note omits the nearest grammatical alternative: niyatam as n. nom. sg. agreeing with idam ('and this supreme, purifying, established/ordained [work]'), which needs no change of form. The rejected alternative it does give (niyatena) is a red herring.

patch.text: A second alternative: niyatam as n. nom. sg. agreeing with idam ('this supreme, purifying, ordained [work]'), with no change of form; also as adverb it may mean 'regularly, constantly' rather than 'assuredly'. Medium confidence stands.

issues.problem: vibuddha is the final member and a past participle ('awakened/enlightened by not-one, i.e. many, systems'): an instrumental tat-puruṣa, not a bahuvrīhi.

'without pause' is not a meaning of anāgata (an-āgata = 'not come, not arrived; future; unforeseen'). The draft admits the word is unclear but then asserts an invented sense in gloss, Hindi ('बिना रुके') and English ('without pause'). The form is most simply n. acc. sg. agreeing with saṃdarbham ('the composition ... which had not [previously] come into being'); an adverbial 'in advance / beforehand' (future-looking, cf. dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā in 33) is the other defensible option. Neither supports 'without pause'.

issues.problem: An unsourced 'some versions read' is exactly the invented-variant pattern the brief forbids. The sadotthāyī reading belongs to the parallel verse in the Ādiparvan (tribhir varṣaiḥ sadotthāyī kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ ...), not to a witness of this line; say so or drop it. Rewrite the note to match the corrected reading.

patch.value: anāgatam is doubtful here. Taken as n. acc. sg. agreeing with saṃdarbham: 'the composition (of this Bhārata) that had not yet come into being'. Alternative: adverbial 'in advance, beforehand' (he composed, with divine sight, what was still to come). 'Without pause' has no lexical support. The parallel verse in the Ādiparvan reads tribhir varṣaiḥ sadotthāyī ('ever diligent') instead; that is a different verse, not a variant of this line.

issues.problem: The key word has no settled sense and the translation depends on it.

summary: 58 units reviewed (54 verses, 4 speaker lines); 11 units get 'fix', 47 'ok'. 1 error-severity issue: unit 41, where the draft turns the doubtful anāgatam into an invented sense 'without pause' in gloss, Hindi and English and cites an unsourced 'some versions read' (the sadotthāyī reading is the Ādiparvan parallel, not a witness of this line); patches give the literal reading, a corrected note and confidence low. Unit 31 (niyatam): the adverb reading and the supplied 'composed' are acceptable and honestly noted; patch adds the missed n. nom. sg. alternative agreeing with idam and tidies the Hindi; medium confidence stands. Remaining issues are minor: Hindi word choice (6 ब्रह्मर्षि→विप्रर्षि, 8 पुराण→पुरातन), a supplied 'मुनि' in 7, an added 'ही' in 49, a double ergative in 46, two gram labels (19 divam f., 33 tat-puruṣa), a garbled gloss in 15, and a missing alternative construal in 23. Token coverage, sandhi, name lists and the long verses 50 and 54 are sound; no regrouping suggested. Glossary additions for consistency across chunks: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana (कृष्ण द्वैपायन), Vyāsa (व्यास), Śaunaka (शौनक), sūta = the Sūta (सूत), itihāsa kept as itihāsa (इतिहास), Jaya (जय).
